Jacobin.title: The Political Economy of Cognitive Dissonance
Jacobin.summary: Cognitive dissonance helps explain why people often turn away from problems they feel powerless to change: denial takes hold. That denial can weaken the solidarity required to change the conditions that leave people feeling powerless.

Jacobin.title: Jacobin Is International

Jacobin.title: The Video Game Industry’s Crisis Is a Crisis of Capitalism
Jacobin.summary: Recurring layoffs reveal an industry organized around extracting value while workers bear the cost of crises. In Montreal, game workers are building solidarity and organizing for collective power.

Jacobin.title: Anwar Shaikh Changed My Life
Jacobin.summary: Economist Anwar Shaikh, who died this month, spent half a century turning Marx’s categories into hard numbers. His first teaching assistant and longtime collaborator remembers the man and the work.

Jacobin.title: Tax the Rich and Slash the Military Budget
Jacobin.summary: The Left is often asked how it proposes to pay for programs like universal childcare, Medicare or All, and a green jobs program. Here’s how: tax wealth and capital the same way we already tax wages, and slash our bloated and destructive military budget.

Jacobin.title: The Political Economy of the Restaurant
Jacobin.summary: Political organizer and chef Lewis Bassett’s The Full English offers a firsthand account of how English food has been shaped by industrialization, empire, and class from the vantage point of restaurants across the country.

Jacobin.title: Workers Can Govern, but They Need Power First
Jacobin.summary: A new book makes the most rigorous case yet for why so few working-class people hold office. But by treating the lack of workers in office as a law of electoral democracy, its authors underrate how much organized workers could change it.

Jacobin.title: The Left Needs an Answer to the Center’s New Cold War Program
